quote: Lemma 4.14. (Müller and Scarsini, 2000) Let X, Y be two bivariate random vectors and have the same marginals, then X ≤sm Y is equivalent to X ≤uo Y.

hypotheses.text: X, Y bivariate with same marginals

conclusion.direction: X ≤_sm Y ⟺ X ≤_uo Y (supermodular = upper orthant in bivariate case)

quote: Theorem 4.10. Let Y1, Y2 follow (18). The following statements are true: (1) If µ1 = µ2, δ1 = δ2 and Σ2 ≥ Σ1, then Y1 ≤dcx Y2. (2) If µ1 = µ2, then Y1 ≤dcx Y2 if and only if δ1 = δ2 and Σ2 ≥ Σ1. (3) If δ1 = δ2, then Y1 ≤dcx Y2 if and only if µ1 = µ2 and Σ2 ≥ Σ1.
compared: Y1 vs Y2 in directionally convex order

hypotheses.text: µ1 = µ2, δ1 = δ2, Σ2 ≥ Σ1 (p.s.d. in the stated direction)

quote: Theorem 4.11. Let Y1, Y2 follow (18). The following statements hold: (1) If µ1 = µ2, δ1 = δ2, σ1,ii ≤ σ2,ii for 1 ≤ i ≤ n and σ1,ij = σ2,ij for 1 ≤ i < j ≤ n, then Y1 ≤ccx Y2. (2) If µ1 = µ2, then Y1 ≤ccx Y2 if and only if δ1 = δ2, σ1,ii ≤ σ2,ii for 1 ≤ i ≤ n and σ1,ij = σ2,ij for 1 ≤ i < j ≤ n. (3) If δ1 = δ2, then Y1 ≤ccx Y2 if and only if µ1 = µ2, σ1,ii ≤ σ2,ii for 1 ≤ i ≤ n and σ1,ij = σ2,ij for 1 ≤ i < j ≤ n.
compared: Y1 vs Y2 in componentwise convex order

hypotheses.text: equal means/skews; diagonal variances ordered; equal off-diagonals

quote: Theorem 4.12. Let Y1, Y2 follow (18). Y1 ≤sm Y2 if and only if Y1 and Y2 have the same marginals and σ1,ij ≤ σ2,ij for all 1 ≤ i < j ≤ n.
compared: Y1 vs Y2 in supermodular order

hypotheses.text: same marginals (µ1 = µ2, δ1 = δ2, σ1,ii = σ2,ii); σ1,ij ≤ σ2,ij for i < j

conclusion.direction: Y1 ≤_sm Y2 iff same marginals and σ1,ij ≤ σ2,ij

quote: Theorem 4.15. Let Y1, Y2 follow (18). The following statements are true: (1) If µ2 + β(z)δ2 ≥ µ1 + β(z)δ1 for all z, σ1,ii = σ2,ii for all 1 ≤ i ≤ n and σ1,ij ≤ σ2,ij for all 1 ≤ i ≠ j ≤ n, then Y1 ≤uo Y2. (2) If Y1 ≤uo Y2 and g satisfies Assumption 4.1, then µ1 + E(β(Z))δ1 ≤ µ2 + E(β(Z))δ2 and σ1,ii = σ2,ii for all 1 ≤ i ≤ n. (3) If Y1 and Y2 have the same marginals and Y1 ≤uo Y2, then σ1,ij ≤ σ2,ij for all 1 ≤ i < j ≤ n.
compared: Y1 vs Y2 in upper orthant order

conclusion.direction: Y1 ≤_uo Y2 (sufficiency); necessity of mean-type inequality, equal diagonal variances and σ-inequalities

quote: Theorem 4.16. Let Y1, Y2 follow (18). The following statements are true: (1) If µ1 = µ2, δ1 = δ2 and Σ2 − Σ1 is copositive, then Y1 ≤cp Y2. (2) If µ1 = µ2, then Y1 ≤cp Y2, if and only if δ1 = δ2 and Σ2 − Σ1 is copositive. (3) If δ1 = δ2, then Y1 ≤cp Y2, if and only if µ1 = µ2 and Σ2 − Σ1 is copositive.
compared: Y1 vs Y2 in copositive order

quote: Theorem 4.17. Let Y1, Y2 follow (18). The following statements are true: (1) If µ1 = µ2, δ1 = δ2 and Σ2 − Σ1 is completely positive, then Y1 ≤cop Y2. (2) If µ1 = µ2, then Y1 ≤cop Y2, if and only if δ1 = δ2 and Σ2 − Σ1 is completely positive. (3) If δ1 = δ2, then Y1 ≤cop Y2, if and only if µ1 = µ2 and Σ2 − Σ1 is completely positive.
compared: Y1 vs Y2 in completely positive order

quote: Theorem 4.6. Let Y1, Y2 follow (18). We have the following conclusions: (1) If µ1 = µ2, δ1 = δ2 and Σ2 − Σ1 is positive semi-definite, then Y1 ≤cx (≤lcx, ≤ilcx) Y2. (2) If µ1 = µ2, then Y1 ≤cx (≤lcx, ≤ilcx) Y2 if and only if δ1 = δ2 and Σ2 − Σ1 is positive semi-definite. (3) If δ1 = δ2, then Y1 ≤cx (≤lcx, ≤ilcx) Y2 if and only if µ1 = µ2 and Σ2 − Σ1 is positive semi-definite.
compared: Y1 vs Y2 in convex / linear convex / increasing linear convex orders

conclusion.direction: Y1 ≤_cx (≤_lcx, ≤_ilcx) Y2; iff statements under common means/skews

ambiguity: lcx = linear convex order; ilcx = increasing linear convex order (Definition 2.5).

quote: Theorem 4.9. Let Y1, Y2 follows (18). The following results hold: (1) If µ2 + β(z)δ2 ≥ µ1 + β(z)δ1 for all z and Σ2 − Σ1 is positive semi-definite, then Y1 ≤icx (≤iplcx) Y2. (2) If Y1 ≤icx (≤iplcx) Y2 and the corresponding density generator g1 of a^T Y1 satisfies Assumption 4.2 for all a ∈ R^n_+, then µ2 + Eβ(Z)δ2 ≥ µ1 + Eβ(Z)δ1 and Σ2 − Σ1 is copositive.

quote: Example 4.4. We consider the special case of univariate GLSE distribution to illustrate the results in Lemma 4.3. The survival functions of the GHSS distributions under three parameter setting are plotted in Figure 1(a). It is easy to check that the conditions in Lemma 4.3(1) are satisfied, and thus agrees with the usual stochastic ordering among these three distributions displayed in the plot. Moreover, Figure 1(b) provides a counterexample showing that the survival functions of these distributions cross with each other if the scale parameters of the three distributions are not identical.

hypotheses.text: Lemma 4.3(1) conditions hold in Figure 1(a); violated σ-equality in Figure 1(b)

conclusion.direction: st ordering verified in (a); survival curves cross in (b) when σ's differ
